article_title: Northern Humboldt Union High School District: "Aligning Mental Health Initiatives with a Multi-Tiered System of Supports through Project Cal-Well"
citation: Northern Humboldt Union High School District: Aligning Mental Health Initiatives With a Multi-Tiered System of Supports Through Project Cal-Well. (2024). WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Grant matrix aligning district school-based mental health grants and initiatives
description: NHUHSD created a grant matrix to align its many school-based mental health grants, projects, and initiatives. "By tracking all of this information in one physical document, NHUHSD leadership can better understand its assets and how various activities align with each other and be intentional when making decisions about adopting new practices." The tool supports coordination and sustainability planning across the 5-year grant period.
requirements: Tracking of all grants and initiatives in one physical document maintained by district leadership
target_learners: district leaders coordinating school mental health initiatives
target_learning_goals: aligning and sustaining school mental health services
examples: Used throughout the 5-year Project Cal-Well grant to align additional sustainability grants
key_sources: Northern Humboldt Union High School District: Aligning Mental Health Initiatives With a Multi-Tiered System of Supports Through Project Cal-Well. (2024). WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED655969

article_title: Integrating performance assessments across a PK-20 continuum: A locally developed collaboration
citation: McCurdy, K., Reagan, E. M., Schram, T., & Rogers, A. (2018). Integrating performance assessments across a PK-20 continuum: A locally developed collaboration. Education Policy Analysis Archives, 26(14). http://dx.doi.org/10.14507/epaa.26.3437
title: New Hampshire Teacher Candidate Assessment of Performance (NH TCAP)
description: The NH TCAP is a teacher candidate performance assessment adopted in 2013 by a consortium of teacher educators across all New Hampshire institutions of higher education "to support teacher candidate learning and assess readiness to teach." It was adapted from the Performance Assessment for California Teachers for the state context, with agreed implementation issues including scorer training, instructor involvement, and consequentiality. It is housed at the institutional level, is one of multiple measures determining readiness to teach, and is intended to keep evolving as data are collected and analyzed.
requirements: Consortium agreement around key implementation issues such as facilitation with teacher candidates, scorer training, instructor involvement and assistance, and the consequential nature of the assessment
constraints: It is housed at the institutional level and determined by the institutions, in contrast to other teacher candidate performance assessments across the country
target_learners: preservice teacher candidates in New Hampshire institutions of higher education
target_learning_goals: teacher candidate learning and readiness to teach
examples: In 2013 a consortium of teacher educators across all New Hampshire institutions of higher education adopted the NH TCAP, adapting the Performance Assessment for California Teachers (Pecheone & Chung, 2006) for the state context
key_sources: McCurdy, K., Reagan, E. M., Schram, T., & Rogers, A. (2018). Integrating performance assessments across a PK-20 continuum: A locally developed collaboration. Education Policy Analysis Archives, 26(14). http://dx.doi.org/10.14507/epaa.26.3437

article_title: Creative Thinking Ability to Increase Student Mathematical of Junior High School by Applying Models Numbered Heads Together
citation: Lince, R. (2016). Creative Thinking Ability to Increase Student Mathematical of Junior High School by Applying Models Numbered Heads Together. Journal of Education and Practice, 7(6), 206-212. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1098210
title: Numbered Heads Together cooperative learning structure with numbered group members and random caller
description: Numbered Heads Together is a cooperative learning model that emphasizes a special structure designed to influence student interaction patterns and improve mastery. Students are divided into groups and each member is numbered. The teacher poses a task or question, groups discuss to find the best answer and ensure all members know it, then the teacher "calls one randomly" and that student presents the group's answer. Because the teacher "did not tell in advance who will represent the group," all students must be prepared, ensuring total involvement and increasing responsibility in group discussions.
requirements: Students are divided into groups with each student numbered
The teacher randomly calls one student per group to present the group's answer
constraints: Not very appropriate when the number of students is large because it takes a long time
Not all group members may be called by the teacher due to limited time
examples: In this study, class VIII1 (34 students) learned with NHT while class VIII2 (34 students) learned conventionally at SMPN 4 in Ambon
key_sources: Lince, R. (2016). Creative Thinking Ability to Increase Student Mathematical of Junior High School by Applying Models Numbered Heads Together. Journal of Education and Practice, 7(6), 206-212. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1092494

article_title: Creative Thinking Ability to Increase Student Mathematical of Junior High School by Applying Models Numbered Heads Together
citation: Lince, R. (2016). Creative Thinking Ability to Increase Student Mathematical of Junior High School by Applying Models Numbered Heads Together. Journal of Education and Practice, 7(6), 206-212. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1098210
title: Use NHT cooperative learning as an alternative model to enhance mathematical creative thinking ability
description: The article recommends applying the Numbered Heads Together model as an alternative learning approach to enhance students' mathematical creative thinking ability. NHT requires active student participation, helps improve learning achievement and attitudes toward mathematics, and its structured stages (numbering, questioning, group discussion, random answering) align with different aspects of creative thinking. The study's conclusion states that "Learning with NHT more suitable to enhance the students' ability to think creatively mathematically" than conventional learning.
requirements: Teachers must implement the NHT stages consistently, including group numbering, questioning, group discussion, and random calling
constraints: The improvement, while better than conventional learning, remained in the medium category per Hake's criteria
examples: The study applied NHT to class VIII1 (34 students) and compared results with conventionally taught class VIII2 (34 students) at SMPN 4 Ambon during the 2014/2015 school year
key_sources: Lince, R. (2016). Creative Thinking Ability to Increase Student Mathematical of Junior High School by Applying Models Numbered Heads Together. Journal of Education and Practice, 7(6), 206-212. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1092494

article_title: The power of simulation: a large-scale narrative analysis of learners' experiences.
citation: Bearman Margaret, Greenhill Jennene, Nestel Debra. (2019). The power of simulation: a large‐scale narrative analysis of learners’ experiences. Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/medu.13747
title: NHET-Sim national faculty development programme and its reflective-prompt narrative dataset
description: The National Health and Education Training Simulation (NHET-Sim) programme has since 2011 provided "thousands of health and social care professionals across Australia with the introductory skills and concepts necessary to facilitate SBE". Its introductory module includes an online reflective prompt — describe the most powerful learning experience you have had using simulation — from which the study extracted 327 narratives from 2624 consenting participants (52% of 5033 completers between October 2012 and January 2015). Contributors were predominantly nursing (56%) and medicine (24%), average age 44 years.
requirements: Participants complete the introductory module's online reflections, which activate prior learning and practice contexts
constraints: The dataset came from participant logs intended as reflections, not narratives, and participants may hold more positive views of education than the general health professional population
target_learners: Health and social care professionals across Australia undertaking simulation educator training
target_learning_goals: Introductory skills and concepts necessary to facilitate simulation-based education
examples: The study analysed 327 narratives meeting Reese et al.'s minimum criteria for context, chronology and theme
key_sources: Bearman Margaret, Greenhill Jennene, Nestel Debra. (2019). The power of simulation: a large‐scale narrative analysis of learners’ experiences. Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1111/medu.13747
